podcast.title: Brill Building Duo
podcast.body: Gerry Goffin was part of the famed Brill Building Duo with Carole King, a songwriting partnership responsible for a string of hits for various artists in the 1960s. "The Brill Building Duo, who'd penned such hits as the Cherelles Will You Love Me Tomorrow, Little Eva's The Locomotion, and the chiffon's One Fine Day."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: First Husband of Carole King
podcast.body: Gerry Goffin met Carole King in college and became her first husband. By the time King was 17, they were married and expecting their first child. "Someone else she met while at college was the man who was to rick on her first husband, another Jerry, Jerry Goughin."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.title: Initial Dislike of Rock and Roll
podcast.body: Goffin initially disliked rock and roll music due to what he perceived as its "lyrical vacuity." His work on "Will You Love Me Tomorrow" allowed him to develop a lyrical formula for girl groups that introduced greater emotional depth to pop music. "Goffin's initial dislike of rock and roll music had been because of what he perceived as his lyrical vacuity, and in Will you love me tomorrow, he found a lyrical formula that would define girl groups from that point on."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Musical Ambitions and Limitations
podcast.body: Goffin had attempted to write a musical, but he primarily excelled as a lyricist and struggled with the musical aspects of composition. He became keen to write with Carole King after learning she was selling songs. "He'd been trying to write a musical, but he was primarily a live assist and couldn't do much with music."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.title: Songwriting Contract with Aldon Music
podcast.body: Along with Carole King, Gerry Goffin was signed by Al Nevins and Don Kirshner of Aldon Music to a three-year songwriting contract. The contract included advances of $1,000, $2,000, and $3,000 for consecutive years, offset against their royalties, which was a fortune for the young couple. "When Caval King played them a few of the songs she co-written with Goffin, they signed Goffin and King to a three-year contract, with advances of $1,000 for the first year, $2,000 for the second, and $3,000 for the third, to be offset against their royalties."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
